name: Google Compute Engine A2 (NVIDIA A100 40GB / 80GB)
price_basis: per A100 GPU-hour. a2-ultragpu-8g = 8x A100 80GB at $40.550383123/instance-hr / 8 = $5.0688 (the 80GB part with 1,360GB RAM). a2-highgpu-8g = 8x A100 at $29.38708/8 = $3.6734 (40GB part). a2-highgpu-1g = 1x A100 at $3.673385. Prices as published 2026-10-03.
notes: A2 is the one GPU family in this slice that is both broadly available AND publishes a clean single-GPU shape - a2-highgpu-1g at $3.67/h, no 8-GPU minimum, no allocation ritual. Note the a2-ultragpu vs a2-highgpu distinction is 80GB vs 40GB memory AND a very different RAM/GPU ratio (170GB vs 85GiB per GPU), not a size bump of one instance; ultragpu costs 38% more per GPU-hour. The published 1-year and 3-year CUD columns for a2-highgpu are internally consistent ($2.31 1yr, $1.29 3yr, both under the $3.67 on-demand) so the a2 discount ladder can be trusted where the a3 one could not. Accelerator-optimized machines are excluded from SUDs and flexible CUDs per the same GCP page. Spot is published as N/A for every a2 shape - so unlike AWS, there is no spot escape hatch for A2 on this page, and the discount channel is purely the 1yr/3yr commitment.
